prompt.alinti: Most people ask Claude 'is my idea any good?' and get a polite list of ten pros and cons that flatters them into building the wrong thing. You can instead set up a four-agent council that roasts your idea before you waste six months on it. Each agent has ONE lens, they all argue about the SAME idea, and a judge has to pick a side.
Here’s how to set it up. You drop your idea in one paragraph and it splits it into four people who fight it out.
The believer makes the strongest case for why this works and who desperately needs it.
The skeptic attacks every weak point: who won’t pay, the competitor you forgot, the part you're lying to yourself about.
The investor cares about one thing, whether real money would actually show up and how fast.
Then the judge reads the whole fight and hands you one verdict.
And this is the part that matters. And it remembers your idea so tomorrow you can come back and ask what changed.
People are running ideas through this before they tell a single friend and catching the fatal flaw in 10 minutes instead of six months.
I put together the exact four agent council with every prompt, so comment roast.
